Maintenance Report — MNT-0147-002

Asset: WELL-0147 (NE-07 Well 147, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 18 Feb 2023 08:00 · Finished: 22 Feb 2023 07:00 · Well stopped for this job: 95 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price, Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0147-0016 on 2023-02-16 Report written: 24 Feb 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0147-0016 showed the wellhead at 10.5 °C with the air at 8.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 6 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 264 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 211 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0147-002 (WS-06).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0147-007

Asset: WELL-0147 (NE-07 Well 147, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 25 Jun 2023 08:00 · Finished: 12 Jul 2023 00:00 · Well stopped for this job: 400 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0147-0033 on 2023-06-22 Report written: 13 Jul 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0147-0033 showed the wellhead at 40.6 °C with the air at 35.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 15 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 4 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0147-0042 showed the wellhead at 33.3 °C with the air at 29.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 3 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0147-010

Asset: WELL-0147 (NE-07 Well 147, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 07 Oct 2023 08:00 · Finished: 01 Nov 2023 01:00 · Well stopped for this job: 593 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0147-0048 on 2023-10-05 Report written: 01 Nov 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator found an oil puddle under the gearbox. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0147-0048 showed the wellhead at 27.4 °C with the air at 27.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 23 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Seal wear, made worse by heat and a low oil level. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's pump jack in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0147-010 (WS-06).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0147-016

Asset: WELL-0147 (NE-07 Well 147, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 02 Aug 2024 08:00 · Finished: 03 Aug 2024 04:00 · Well stopped for this job: 20 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward, Brian Coleman · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0147-0090 on 2024-08-01 Report written: 04 Aug 2024

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0147-0090 at 12:00 on 2024-08-01 found crude oil on the pad: about 3.4% of the pad area, estimated 1.6 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 5.5 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 264 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 211 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 1.2 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0147-016 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.48% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).
